title: Before adding a new table or a new in-memory flag, check whether an existing telemetry/dedup table c
trigger: Needing to deduplicate or cache a non-atom concept (a whole session's context blob, a computed aggregate, etc.) against something already tracked in an atom-shaped table like session_deliveries.
behavior_delta: Before adding a new table or a new in-memory flag, check whether an existing telemetry/dedup table can be reused by inserting a sentinel key (e.g. atom_id = '__session_context__') that never collides with a real id. src/hooks/session-start.js does this to dedupe the full SessionStart advisory blob against session_deliveries (built for per-atom delivery tracking) instead of adding a parallel mechanism, and inherits its existing recency window, its clearSessionDeliveries cleanup on compact/clear, and its retention pruning for free. Document the reuse with a one-line comment where the sentinel is defined, since a future reader joining that table against memory_atoms would otherwise wrongly assume every row names a real atom.
what: Before adding a new table or a new in-memory flag, check whether an existing telemetry/dedup table can be reused by inserting a sentinel key (e.g. atom_id = '__session_context__') that never collides with a real id. src/hooks/session-start.js does this to dedupe the full SessionStart advisory blob against session_deliveries (built for per-atom delivery tracking) instead of adding a parallel mechanism, and inherits its existing recency window, its clearSessionDeliveries cleanup on compact/clear, and its retention pruning for free. Document the reuse with a one-line comment where the sentinel is defined, since a future reader joining that table against memory_atoms would otherwise wrongly assume every row names a real atom.
why: Found while implementing a fix for SessionStart resending its full project-context blob on every reconnect: reusing session_deliveries with a sentinel id was safer and cheaper than guessing at harness-specific `source` values or building a second dedup path, and it degrades correctly (falls back to the old always-send behavior) on any harness whose session_id semantics differ or are absent.

evidence_refs.summary: buildSessionStartContext uses SESSION_CONTEXT_ATOM_ID as a sentinel row in session_deliveries to dedupe the advisory blob across reconnects.
session_deliveries's wasDelivered/markDelivered/clearSessionDeliveries have no foreign key on atom_id, so a sentinel string is a safe reuse.
